newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to implement planned incentives for industry.
newsitem.headline: Italy to implement planned incentives for industry.

text.p: Italian industry minister Pier Luigi Bersani said the government would rapidly deploy funds already earmarked by law as incentives to boost industries facing flagging consumer demand, a ministry source said.
Bersani told metalworkers and engineering union leaders at a meeting earlier on Thursday the funds, already set aside by the state, would total a net five to six trillion lire next year.
There were no immediate details about how the funds would be used or which specific sectors were affected.
Provision for the aid is already part of a law covering incentives for economically depressed areas and is also included in the 1997 budget bill, currently before parliament.
The ministry source said Bersani also underlined the need to rebuild a climate of confidence to boost consumer spending, but he did not go into details.
